description: The full log record of one past API call by its request id. Every response carries its id in the X-Request-Id header (and error bodies carry it too), so this is the tool for debugging a failed or slow scrape: it shows status, error_code/error_detail, attempts, the engine and proxy (tier, country, provider, sticky) actually used, whether and how the target blocked it (vendor/signal/rule), per-stage latency spans and credits charged. Returns not_found both for unknown ids and for ones older than your retention window, and for another project's request unless your key has the `read` scope.

id.description: The request id (a ULID, from X-Request-Id or a spicrawl_requests_list row's `id`).

name: spicrawl_request_get

blocked.description: Present only when a bot challenge was detected.

created_at.description: When the request arrived, RFC 3339 UTC.

credits_micro.description: Credits charged in micro-credits (1 credit = 1000000); 0 unless success.

engine.description: The rendering tier that served it: fetch, js or browser. Absent when refused before a tier was chosen.

error_code.description: The problem code the caller got, e.g. ERR::UPSTREAM::CHALLENGE. Absent on success.

http_status.description: The target's HTTP status; absent when no response was received.

proxy.description: What proxy was asked for versus what served. Never an exit IP or credentials.

country.description: Where the exit actually served from; compare with requested_country.

endpoints.description: Every exit touched, in attempt order.

spans.description: Latency in milliseconds per stage; null means not measured. Stages do not sum to total_ms.

queue_ms.description: Wait for a slot; high means capacity shortage, not a slow page.

status.description: Terminal outcome: success, failed, timeout, blocked, rejected or cancelled. Only success is charged.

title: Get one request
